land.text: Lagos, ceded by Oba Dosunmu in the Lagos Treaty of Cession, 6 August 1861

successors.note: The lagos-colony dossier written in the same batch names this kingdom as its predecessor.

capitals.name: Lagos
capitals.note: The Oba page: the Oba's 'official residence since 1630 is Iga Idunganran'; the gazetteer's Lagos point stands for Lagos Island.

correction.text: Lagos (Eko) on its island in the lagoon, with the mainland shore the pages tie to it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Neither page gives an area or a frontier; a 25 km circle round Lagos, the same footprint as the successor lagos-colony shape, stands for the island kingdom. The Oba page names the Oba 'Eleko of Eko'. Start year 1630 is the first entry of the Oba page's reign list (Ado, 1630-1669); the same page's infobox says 'Formation: 1716' and the History page says Lagos was founded 'in the 16th-century by the Awori people', so the founding is not settled.

region.text: Lagos Island and the shore round it

ledger.note: 1630: Ado, 'first King of Lagos', opens the Oba page's reign list (1630-1669); the infobox says 'Formation: 1716' and the History page dates the Awori founding of Lagos to the 16th century. Page conflict: 1630 is the earliest dated reign, not a founding date.

Eko under Benin: Ashipa, an Awori chief, 'was appointed ruler of Eko by the Oba of Benin' and 'initiated a payment of tribute that would not be abolished until 1830'; the Oba page says 'Ashipa was sent to govern Lagos on the Oba of Benin's behalf'. Page silent on the year Ashipa was appointed (Benin attacked Iddo c. 1600); entered at the start of the reign list. The History page calls the subservience 'mostly nominal' by the 18th century. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): the Oba of Lagos list does date Ashipa, 'not crowned', 1600-1630, so the Benin tie may start c. 1600; benin-empire now carries the mirror vassal events (1630, 1830).

c. 1830: Lagos stops paying tribute to Benin. History page: tribute 'would not be abolished until 1830'; Oba page: tribute to Benin continued until 'around the year 1830, when Lagos stopped it'. The Oba page also says the 28 December 1851 defeat of Kosoko 'ended tributary ties to Benin' and that Benin held 'the undisputed right to crown or confirm' Lagos's chosen king; 1830 is followed.

6 August 1861: Oba Dosunmu signs the Lagos Treaty of Cession (30 July 1861 he met Commander Bedingfield aboard HMS Prometheus; he 'resisted the terms of the treaty but under the threat to unleash a bombardment on Lagos' relented). Lagos was declared a colony on 5 March 1862.
6 August 1861: the Kingdom of Lagos ends as a sovereign state with the cession (the Oba dynasty continues as Obas of Lagos).

wars.name: Bombardment of Lagos
belligerents: British naval force with Oba Akitoye
wars.outcome: British victory on 28 December 1851: Oba Kosoko defeated, Akitoye restored under British protection and, in 1852, a treaty abolishing the slave trade (the Consular Period).
wars.note: The Oba page puts the defeat on 28 December 1851; the History page calls the event the 'Bombardment of Lagos or Capture of Lagos'. Kosoko (1845-1851) and Akitoye (1841-1845, 1851-1853) were rival claimants; the page gives no battle sites.

certainty.note: No frontier on either page; a circle round Lagos.

sources.title: History of Lagos
sources.note: Awori founding in the 16th century; Ashipa appointed by the Oba of Benin, tribute abolished 1830; Akinsemoyin; 1851 bombardment; 30 July and 6 August 1861; colony declared 5 March 1862; no area.

sources.title: Oba of Lagos
sources.note: Reign list Ado 1630-1669 to Dosunmu 1853-1885; infobox formation 1716; tribute to Benin until about 1830; 28 December 1851; Iga Idunganran.

notes: The Kingdom of Lagos has no Cliopatria row. Two pages (the Kingdom_of_Lagos title does not load). Disagreements: founding 1630 (first reign) vs 1716 (infobox) vs 'the 16th century' (History page); Akinsemoyin 1704-1749 on the Oba list vs 'took the throne in the 1760s' on the History page; Benin tribute ended about 1830 (both pages) vs 'ended tributary ties to Benin' on 28 December 1851 (Oba page). The Oba page's reign list has gaps (1749-1775, no Osinlokun, only Eshilokun 1780-1819) and is not entered as rulers. The 1852 treaty (Consular Period) is not read as a protectorate because the pages do not say so. The shape is a 25 km circle at Lagos, not a measured kingdom.
